question: Which 4.100.108 functions implement the Bluetooth service-manager register and get-profile paths?
prototype_hypothesis: service_manager_register(service) registers a Bluetooth service into the per-type slot table; service_manager_get_profile(profile_id) returns the registered profile or asserts/logs when absent.
callsite_evidence: sub_C471CA4 decompiles to the service register path and references '[129][service_manager]: %s service register success' and '[131][service_manager]: %s service had registered', storing the service into the slot table unk_200BC73C indexed by the service-type byte

sub_C471CF4 decompiles to the profile getter and references '[195][service_manager]: %s profile-id:%d is not found, profile:%p' plus the source path ../../frameworks/connectivity/bluetooth/service/profiles/service_manager.c:196, returning the profile callback from the registered service slot
Both use the same slot table base (dword_200BC73C) and the same BT notification helper (sub_C470614) as the 3.101.036 service-manager, and sit in the same XIP cluster
Produced by the multi-layer matcher from the verified 3.101.036 set and confirmed by decompiling the exact 4.100.108 IDB
control_flow_evidence: register fails closed when the slot is already taken (logs 'service had registered' and returns the error)
get_profile calls the profile callback at offset 52 of the registered service, and logs the 'not found' diagnostic before the assert helper when the slot is empty
Both must run in the Bluetooth service context (not a bare loader constructor)
ownership_analysis: The service manager owns the registered service slots; callers must not free a registered service while it is live. get_profile borrows the profile for the duration of the call.
unsafe_assumptions: The slot table layout (unk_200BC73C, 2 words per service type) and the profile callback offset (+52) are exact 4.100.108 layout
The service-type byte and profile-id encodings must match the caller's protocol; not cross-validated against other firmware
recommended_probe: Register a service and fetch its profile through the target-private facade; confirm the success log and the profile callback dispatch.
